candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the 'Lock-Token' header and the 'If' header token values sent to the servlet; JCRWebdavServer.SessionCache.get() reads them via WebdavRequestImpl.getLockToken()/IfHeader.getAllTokens() before any authentication. The session-scoped token value needed for the attack is not secret: it is returned to any reader of the locked node in the PROPFIND DAV:lockdiscovery response (AbstractActiveLock.toXml writes getToken(); JcrActiveLock.getToken()/LockTokenMapper derive it as the constant UUID plus the escaped node identifier) and can also be recomputed from a node identifier obtained from normal repository reads.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked whether the token is secret: for OPEN-scoped locks LockImpl.getLockToken() returns the token only to the holder/admin, and the value shown to others is the SESSIONSCOPED-derived string that does NOT match the registered reference, so open-scoped locks alone do not permit this hijack; the flaw is specific to session-scoped locks, whose registered reference is exactly the publicly derivable token. Checked whether a cache hit still requires credentials: SessionProviderImpl.getSession() is only reached on a cache miss (JCRWebdavServer.SessionCache.get lines 231-237), so a matching token bypasses login entirely. Checked the simple WebDAV server (/repository/*, DavSessionProviderImpl) which logs in per request and has no such cache - not affected. Checked CSRFUtil (only POST with three content types, referrer can be set) and JCRWebdavServerServlet.isPreconditionValid (workspace check passes for null/empty workspace name and If-header check passes without an If header). Checked XML parsers (DavDocumentBuilderFactory, ConfigurationParser, SearchIndex, jcr-commons ParsingContentHandler) for XXE and found them hardened with entity resolvers. Checked lock/transaction/subscription token generation (SecureRandom in core; TxLockManagerImpl/SubscriptionManagerImpl use UUIDs), JNDI use (guarded by JndiRepositoryFactory.JNDI_ENABLED, JCR-5135), DirListingExportHandler output escaping (uses Text.encodeIllegalHTMLCharacters), and QValueFactoryImpl deserialization (local temp files only). Tests are stripped from this snapshot, so no test-based confirmation exists.
candidates.impact: Authentication and authorization bypass: an unauthenticated or low-privileged attacker can operate with the victim's repository session for as long as the session-scoped lock keeps that session cached, i.e., read, modify, move, delete, lock/unlock and query content with the victim's privileges (including administrative sessions). This is cross-user session hijacking/privilege escalation on a network-facing component, and it also allows the attacker to consume/abuse the victim's session rather than just the lock.
candidates.prerequisites: Deployment must expose the JCR WebDAV/JCR-Remoting servlet (jackrabbit-webapp maps org.apache.jackrabbit.j2ee.JcrRemotingServlet at /server/*; the OSGi DavexServletService uses the same base classes). A victim session must currently hold a session-scoped write lock created through that servlet (e.g., a JCR client using spi2dav with Node.lock(deep, true)/RepositoryService.lock(sessionScoped=true)), which keeps the victim's DavSession referenced in the cache until unlock/expiry. The attacker needs to learn the derived token (read access to the locked node via PROPFIND lockdiscovery or knowledge of the node identifier); using the token requires no credentials and no knowledge of the victim's password.
candidates.root_cause: JCRWebdavServer.SessionCache.get() treats request-supplied lock tokens (Lock-Token header and If-header tokens) as bearer handles and returns the cached JCR repository session of whoever registered that token, without any credential check. DefaultItemCollection.lock() registers the DAV lock token of a session-scoped JCR lock as a session reference; for session-scoped locks LockImpl.getLockToken() returns null, so LockTokenMapper.getDavLocktoken() derives the token deterministically as 'opaquelocktoken:4403ef44-4124-11e1-b965-00059a3c7a00:<node identifier>'. That derived token is not a secret: it is embedded in the DAV:lockdiscovery property (AbstractActiveLock.toXml -> JcrActiveLock.getToken()) that is served to every session able to read the locked node, and it can also be recomputed from the node identifier. Combining a non-secret token with token-based session lookup lets any other user (or an unauthenticated client) obtain the lock owner's cached repository session.
candidates.title: Cross-user WebDAV/JCR session hijacking via public session-scoped lock tokens used as session-cache handles
candidates.trace: 1) Victim locks a node through /server/* with a session-scoped lock: DefaultItemCollection.lock() calls LockManager.lock(..., sessionScoped=true) and then getSession().addReference(lock.getToken()) (lines 687-701). lock.getToken() -> LockTokenMapper.getDavLocktoken(): because LockImpl.getLockToken() returns null for session-scoped locks, the DAV token is 'opaquelocktoken:4403ef44-4124-11e1-b965-00059a3c7a00:<nodeId>' and is stored in the cache's referenceToSessionMap keyed to the victim's DavSession. 2) Any other reader of the node issues PROPFIND for DAV:lockdiscovery: AbstractResource.initProperties() adds new LockDiscovery(getLocks()) (line 645) and DefaultItemCollection.getLock() builds a JcrActiveLock for the locked node regardless of who holds it (lines 633-661); serialization writes the derived token into <D:locktoken><D:href> (AbstractActiveLock.toXml lines 72-76; JcrActiveLock.getToken lines 95-104). 3) The attacker sends any request to /server/* with header 'Lock-Token: <stolen token>' (or 'If: (<stolen token>)'). AbstractWebdavServlet.service() calls getDavSessionProvider().attachSession(webdavRequest) before any credential check (lines 286-295); JCRWebdavServer.SessionCache.get() sees the lock token, finds it in referenceToSessionMap and returns the victim's cached DavSession (lines 210-228), which is then attached to the request (WebdavRequestImpl.setDavSession, lines 146-161). 4) The servlet executes the requested method (GET/PROPFIND/PUT/POST ':diff'/DELETE) with JcrDavSession.getRepositorySession() unwrapping the victim's JCR session (JcrRemotingServlet.getRepositorySession, lines 637-640), and JCRWebdavServerServlet.isPreconditionValid()/matchesIfHeader() pass because there is either no If header or the token also matches the resource's lock. JCR-5135-style 'missing-auth-mapping' and the CSRF/referrer check are not obstacles (the latter only applies to POST with urlencoded/multipart/text-plain content and a Referer can be supplied).
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution or exploit was performed, so the hijack is a source-level lead, not a confirmed vulnerability. I could not compare against the upstream fix commit or a CVE record, and I did not inspect the jackrabbit-core persistence/query internals or all 2064 files. Whether a given deployment has a victim holding a live session-scoped lock over /server/* (or the OSGi servlet) and whether anonymous/low-priv users can read the locked node determine real-world exploitability. The exact lifetime of the cached victim session after the lock expires/refresh and multi-instance/clustered behavior were not verified.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper authentication / authorization bypass leading to session hijacking (CWE-287, CWE-384, CWE-639)

coverage_summary: Source scope: 2064 model-visible files under the assigned root (2034 parsed/indexed by the P1 index; 30 files missing from the index, mostly resources/non-Java or build files); no symlinks or over-size files were excluded, and binaries are refused. Tests were removed by the harness, so review is main-source only. I inspected web-facing and security-relevant code: jackrabbit-webdav server/request/header/XML handling, jackrabbit-jcr-server (JCR WebDAV resources, JcrRemotingServlet/JsonDiffHandler, session provider/session cache, locks, import/export handlers), jackrabbit-webapp deployment descriptors and JSPs, jackrabbit-core lock/security/query/config/data store areas, jackrabbit-jcr-commons and jackrabbit-jcr2spi XML handling, jackrabbit-spi-commons value/privilege XML handling, jackrabbit-data, and the parent/module poms. The submitted candidate is the strongest traced issue; the jcr2spi importXML XXE is recorded as an unconfirmed weaker lead.
limitations: No code execution, tests, or scanners were run; the candidate is a source-evidence lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.
Tests were stripped from the snapshot and no git history/patches are available, so I could not diff against the upstream fix or identify a CVE record for this code.
The P1 index is syntactic only (no data/control-flow, no semantic resolution; Spring/security enforcement unverified); every relation label used was re-checked against source text.
30 source files are missing from the P1 index (unsupported/unparsed) and were not navigated via the index; some, but not all, were reviewed by direct text reads (e.g., .jsp/.xml/resources).

Coverage is not exhaustive across all 2064 files (large modules such as persistence managers, cluster, data store internals, standalone CLI commands, and OSGi integration code were sampled rather than fully traced).
Exploitability depends on deployment specifics (exposed /server/* endpoint, a victim holding a session-scoped lock, attacker read access to the locked node) that could not be verified at runtime.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE in jackrabbit-jcr2spi SessionImpl.importXML: SessionImpl builds its own static SAXParserFactory with only namespaceAware (lines 114-119) and parses caller-supplied XML with an ImportHandler that extends DefaultHandler without overriding resolveEntity (lines 397-421; jackrabbit-jcr2spi/xml/ImportHandler.java extends DefaultHandler), unlike jcr-commons ParsingContentHandler whose resolveEntity returns an empty stream. This is a plausible XXE (CWE-611) but it is client/library-side only (the repository core and WorkspaceImpl paths use the hardened ParsingContentHandler; the default webapp repository uses jackrabbit-core, not jcr2spi), so impact requires an embedding application to import attacker-controlled XML; ranked weaker than the session-cache issue.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only where an application uses a jcr2spi-based Session/RepositoryImpl and passes untrusted XML to importXML; no server-side path in the standard webapp/standalone deployment was traced, so the security impact is conditional on the embedding application.

rejected_leads.lead: jackrabbit-jcr-server DavexServletService (OSGi) sets INIT_PARAM_CSRF_PROTECTION = CSRFUtil.DISABLED (line 52), disabling referrer-based CSRF protection by default.
rejected_leads.reason: Configuration/hardening gap that openly assumes a site-wide CSRF filter; not a standalone exploitable vulnerability in the source snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Session-scoped DAV lock tokens are derived from node identifiers (LockTokenMapper) and exposed through lockdiscovery to non-holders.
rejected_leads.reason: This is the enabler for the submitted candidate, not a separate root cause; reported together with the session-cache session retrieval.

rejected_leads.lead: JNDI lookup paths in JndiRepositoryFactory/RegistryHelper (JCR-5135 area).
rejected_leads.reason: The snapshot already contains the fix: lookups/registration are guarded by JndiRepositoryFactory.JNDI_ENABLED (jackrabbit-jcr-commons JndiRepositoryFactory lines 57-98; jackrabbit-core jndi/RegistryHelper lines 28, 64-104).

rejected_leads.lead: XPath/query string building in the demo webapp (search.jsp builds an XPath statement from request parameter q).
rejected_leads.reason: Query is executed with the anonymous demo session and the webapp escapes HTML output and single quotes; no privilege boundary is crossed.

summary: Apache Jackrabbit 2.23.2-beta-SNAPSHOT (trunk, ~2025; tests stripped from snapshot). I reviewed the web-facing modules (jackrabbit-webdav, jackrabbit-jcr-server, jackrabbit-webapp, jackrabbit-jcr-servlet), core security/lock/query code, jcr-commons/jcr2spi XML handling, and build/config files. One high-impact, source-evidenced candidate: cross-user session hijacking in the JCR WebDAV/JCR-Remoting server, because the session cache selects a cached repository session purely from an attacker-controllable Lock-Token/If token, while session-scoped lock tokens are not secrets (they are derived from the node identifier and are returned in the DAV:lockdiscovery property to any reader). A secondary, weaker lead (unhardened SAX parser in jcr2spi Session.importXML, XXE) is listed as rejected/unconfirmed. No runtime verification was performed.
